translations.literal: Gentleman-in-Attendance Commandant Geng Bing several times submitted requesting attack on the Xiongnu; the emperor because Illustrious Kin Marquis Dou Gu had once followed his father's elder brother Rong in Hexi and clearly knew border affairs, therefore had Bing, Gu, Grand Master of the Stud Ji Tong, Tiger-Gallant Center Commandant Ma Liao, Marquis of Xiabo Liu Zhang, Marquis of Haozhi Geng Zhong, and others jointly deliberate it.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman-in-Attendance Commandant Geng Bing repeatedly memorialized to attack the Xiongnu. Because Illustrious Kin Marquis Dou Gu had followed his uncle Rong in Hexi and knew border affairs well, the emperor had Bing, Gu, Grand Master of the Stud Ji Tong, Tiger-Gallant Center Commandant Ma Liao, Marquis of Xiabo Liu Zhang, Marquis of Haozhi Geng Zhong, and others deliberate the campaign together.

sentences.zh: 耿秉曰：「昔者匈奴援引弓之類，並左衽之屬，故不可得而制。

translations.literal: Geng Bing said: "Formerly the Xiongnu drew on bow-bearing kinds and all left-lapel peoples together—therefore they could not be controlled."
translations.idiomatic: Geng Bing said, "Formerly the Xiongnu drew on bow-bearing peoples and all who wore the left lapel together, and could not be controlled."

sentences.zh: 孝武既得河西四郡及居延、朔方，虜失其肥饒畜兵之地，羌、胡分離；

translations.literal: "Emperor Wu having obtained the four Hexi commanderies and Juyan and Shuofang, the barbarians lost their fat, rich lands for raising troops; Qiang and Hu were separated;"
translations.idiomatic: "After Emperor Wu took the four Hexi commanderies plus Juyan and Shuofang, the barbarians lost their rich lands for raising troops, and the Qiang and Hu were separated;"

sentences.zh: 唯有西域，俄復內屬；

translations.literal: "only the Western Region, shortly again submitted within;"
translations.idiomatic: "only the Western Region soon submitted again;"

sentences.zh: 故呼韓邪單于請事款塞，其勢易乘也。

translations.literal: "therefore Chanyu Huhanxie requested service and knocked at the passes—their momentum was easy to ride."
translations.idiomatic: "therefore Chanyu Huhanxie sought allegiance at the passes, and their momentum was easy to exploit."

sentences.zh: 今有南單于，形勢相似；

translations.literal: "Now there is the Southern Chanyu—the situation is similar;"
translations.idiomatic: "Now there is the Southern Chanyu—the situation is similar;"

sentences.zh: 然西域尚未內屬，北虜未有釁作。

translations.literal: "yet the Western Region has not yet submitted within, and the Northern barbarians have not yet made a breach."
translations.idiomatic: "yet the Western Region has not yet submitted, and the Northern barbarians have not yet given cause for war."

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為當先擊白山，得伊吾，破車師，通使烏孫諸國以斷其右臂；

translations.literal: "Your servant foolishly holds that one should first strike White Mountain, obtain Yiwu, break Cheshi, and send envoys through the Wusun states to cut off their right arm;"
translations.idiomatic: "Your servant holds that we should first strike White Mountain, take Yiwu, break Cheshi, and open relations with the Wusun states to cut off their right arm;"

sentences.zh: 伊吾亦有匈奴南呼衍一部。

translations.literal: "At Yiwu there is also one division of the Xiongnu's southern Huyan."
translations.idiomatic: "At Yiwu there is also a division of the Xiongnu's southern Huyan."

sentences.zh: 破此，復為折其左角，然後匈奴可擊也。

translations.literal: "Breaking this, again one breaks their left horn—then the Xiongnu can be struck."
translations.idiomatic: "Break that, and we break their left horn as well—then the Xiongnu can be struck."

sentences.zh: 」上善其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 議者或以為「今兵出白山，匈奴必並兵相助，又當分其東以離其眾。

translations.literal: Some in the deliberation held that "if troops now go out to White Mountain, the Xiongnu will surely combine forces to assist; one should also divide their east to separate their masses."
translations.idiomatic: Some argued, "If troops go to White Mountain, the Xiongnu will combine to help; we should also divide their eastern forces to split their host."

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，以秉為駙馬都尉，固為奉車都尉；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Bing was made Commandant of the Escort Horse and Gu made Commandant of the Imperial Carriage;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Bing was made Commandant of the Escort Horse and Gu Commandant of the Imperial Carriage;

sentences.zh: 以騎都尉秦彭為秉副，耿忠為固副，皆置從事、司馬，出屯涼州。

translations.literal: Cavalry Commandant Qin Peng was made Bing's deputy and Geng Zhong Gu's deputy; all were given Attendants and Majors and went out to garrison at Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry Commandant Qin Peng was made Bing's deputy and Geng Zhong Gu's deputy; each was given attendants and majors, and they encamped in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 秉，國之子；

translations.literal: Bing was Guo's son;
translations.idiomatic: Bing was Guo's son;

sentences.zh: 忠，弇之子；

translations.literal: Zhong was Yan's son;
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was Yan's son;

sentences.zh: 廖，援之子也。

translations.literal: Liao was Yuan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Liao was Yuan's son.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，遣肜與度遼將軍吳棠將河東、西河羌、胡及南單于兵萬一千騎出高闕塞，竇固、耿忠率酒泉、敦煌、張掖甲卒及盧水羌、胡萬二千騎出酒泉塞，耿秉、秦彭率武威、隴西、天水募士及羌、胡萬騎出張掖居延塞，騎都尉來苗、護烏桓校尉文穆將太原、雁門、代郡、上谷、漁陽、右北平、定襄郡兵及烏桓、鮮卑萬一千騎出平城塞，伐北匈奴。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, Tong was sent with Crossing-the-Liao General Wu Tang to lead Hedong, Xihe, Qiang, Hu, and Southern Chanyu troops—eleven thousand cavalry—out Gaoque Pass; Dou Gu and Geng Zhong led Jiuquan, Dunhuang, and Zhangye armored soldiers plus Lushui Qiang and Hu—twelve thousand cavalry—out Jiuquan Pass; Geng Bing and Qin Peng led Wuwu, Longxi, and Tianshui recruited men plus Qiang and Hu—ten thousand cavalry—out Zhangye Juyan Pass; Cavalry Commandant Lai Miao and Protector of the Wuhuan Commandant Wen Mu led Taiyuan, Yanmen, Dai, Shanggu, Yuyang, Right Beiping, and Dingxiang commandery troops plus Wuhuan and Xianbei—eleven thousand cavalry—out Pingcheng Pass, to attack the Northern Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the second month, Tong was sent with Crossing-the-Liao General Wu Tang leading eleven thousand cavalry of Hedong, Xihe, Qiang, Hu, and the Southern Chanyu out Gaoque Pass; Dou Gu and Geng Zhong led twelve thousand armored men of Jiuquan, Dunhuang, and Zhangye plus Lushui Qiang and Hu out Jiuquan Pass; Geng Bing and Qin Peng led ten thousand recruits of Wuwei, Longxi, and Tianshui plus Qiang and Hu out Zhangye Juyan Pass; Cavalry Commandant Lai Miao and Protector of the Wuhuan Commandant Wen Mu led eleven thousand troops of Taiyuan, Yanmen, Dai, Shanggu, Yuyang, Right Beiping, and Dingxiang plus Wuhuan and Xianbei out Pingcheng Pass—to attack the Northern Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 竇固、耿忠至天山，擊呼衍王，斬首千餘級；

translations.literal: Dou Gu and Geng Zhong reached the Heavenly Mountains, struck the Huyan King, and beheaded more than a thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Gu and Geng Zhong reached the Heavenly Mountains, struck the Huyan King, and took more than a thousand heads;

sentences.zh: 追至蒲類海，取伊吾盧地，置宜禾都尉，留吏士屯田伊吾盧城。

translations.literal: pursued to Pulei Sea, took Yiwulu territory, established the Chief Commandant of Yihe, and left clerks and soldiers to garrison-farm at Yiwulu city.
translations.idiomatic: pursued to Pulei Sea, took Yiwulu, established the Chief Commandant of Yihe, and left officials and soldiers to garrison-farm at Yiwulu.

sentences.zh: 耿秉、秦彭擊匈林王，絕幕六百餘里，至三木樓山而還。

translations.literal: Geng Bing and Qin Peng struck the Hunlin King, crossed the desert more than six hundred li, reached Sanmulou Mountain, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Bing and Qin Peng struck the Hunlin King, crossed the desert more than six hundred li to Sanmulou Mountain, and returned.

sentences.zh: 來苗、文穆至匈河水上，虜皆奔走，無所獲。

translations.literal: Lai Miao and Wen Mu reached the Xiongnu River's waters; the barbarians all fled—nothing was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Miao and Wen Mu reached the Xiongnu River; the enemy fled and they took nothing.

sentences.zh: 祭肜與南匈奴左賢王信不相得，出高闕塞九百餘里，得小山，信妄言以為涿邪山，不見虜而還。

translations.literal: Ji Tong and the Southern Xiongnu Left Worthy King Xin did not get along; going out Gaoque Pass more than nine hundred li they found a small hill; Xin falsely said it was Zhuoye Mountain, saw no barbarians, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Tong and the Southern Xiongnu Left Worthy King Xin quarreled; nine hundred li beyond Gaoque Pass they found a small hill; Xin falsely called it Zhuoye Mountain, saw no enemy, and returned.

sentences.zh: 肜與吳棠坐逗留畏懦，下獄，免。

translations.literal: Tong and Wu Tang were charged with delay and cowardice, imprisoned, and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Tong and Wu Tang were charged with delay and cowardice, imprisoned, and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 肜自恨無功，出獄數日，歐血死。

translations.literal: Tong himself resented having no achievement; several days after leaving prison he vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: Tong, bitter at achieving nothing, vomited blood and died a few days after release.

sentences.zh: 臨終，謂其子曰：「吾蒙國厚恩，奉使不稱，身死誠慚恨，義不可以無功受賞。

translations.literal: At the end he told his son: "I received the state's thick grace; the mission did not fulfill its name—to die is truly shame and regret; righteousness cannot accept reward without achievement."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his son, "I received the state's great grace; the mission failed me—I die in shame; by right one must not take reward without merit."

sentences.zh: 死後，若悉簿上所得物，身自詣兵屯，效死前行，以副吾心。

translations.literal: "After death, if you fully register on the books all goods received, go in person to the military garrison, and offer death advancing forward—to match my heart."
translations.idiomatic: "After my death, register every gift you received, go yourself to the army, and die advancing—that will satisfy my heart."

sentences.zh: 」既卒，其子逢上疏，具陳遺言。

translations.literal: " When he had died, his son Feng submitted a memorial fully stating the last words.
translations.idiomatic: " When he died, his son Feng submitted a memorial setting out these last words.

sentences.zh: 帝雅重肜，方更任用，聞之，大驚，嗟歎良久。

translations.literal: The emperor had greatly esteemed Tong and was just about to employ him again; on hearing this he was greatly startled and sighed long.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had greatly esteemed Tong and was about to employ him again; on hearing this he was deeply shaken and sighed long.

sentences.zh: 烏桓、鮮卑每朝賀京師，常過肜塚拜謁，仰天號泣。

translations.literal: Whenever the Wuhuan and Xianbei came to court audience at the capital they would pass Tong's tomb to bow and visit, looking up to heaven and wailing.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Wuhuan and Xianbei came to court they passed Tong's tomb to bow and wailed to heaven.

sentences.zh: 遼東吏民為立祠，四時奉祭焉。

translations.literal: Officials and people of Liaodong built a shrine for him and offered sacrifice at the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people of Liaodong built him a shrine and sacrificed at the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 竇固獨有功，加位特進。

translations.literal: Dou Gu alone had achievement; his rank was raised to Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Gu alone had merit; his rank was raised to Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 固使假司馬班超與從事郭恂俱使西域。

translations.literal: Gu sent Acting Major Ban Chao and Attendant Guo Xun together as envoys to the Western Region.
translations.idiomatic: Gu sent Acting Major Ban Chao and Attendant Guo Xun as envoys to the Western Region.

sentences.zh: 超行到鄯善，鄯善王廣奉超禮敬甚備，後忽更疏懈。

translations.literal: Chao traveled to Shanshan; King Guang of Shanshan received Chao with very full ritual courtesy, then suddenly became more negligent and slack.
translations.idiomatic: Chao reached Shanshan; King Guang received him with full courtesy, then suddenly grew negligent.

sentences.zh: 超謂其官屬曰：「寧覺廣禮意薄乎？

translations.literal: Chao said to his officials: "Do you not notice Guang's ritual intent has grown thin?"
translations.idiomatic: Chao said to his staff, "Do you not notice Guang's courtesy has grown thin?"

sentences.zh: 」官屬曰：「胡人不能常久，無它故也。

translations.literal: " The officials said: "Barbarians cannot be constant long—no other cause."
translations.idiomatic: " His staff said, "Barbarians cannot be constant long—there is no other cause."

sentences.zh: 」超曰：「此必有北虜使來，狐疑未知所從故也。

translations.literal: " Chao said: "This surely means a Northern barbarian envoy came—they are hesitant and do not know whom to follow."
translations.idiomatic: " Chao said, "A Northern barbarian envoy must have come—they are hesitating whom to follow."

sentences.zh: 明者睹未萌，況已著邪！

translations.literal: "The clear-sighted see before sprouts appear—how much more when it is already evident!"
translations.idiomatic: "The clear-sighted see trouble before it sprouts—how much more when it is already plain!"

sentences.zh: 」乃召侍胡，詐之曰：「匈奴使來數日，今安在乎？

translations.literal: " He thereupon summoned the attending Hu and deceived them, saying: "The Xiongnu envoy came several days ago—where is he now?"
translations.idiomatic: " He summoned the attending Hu and tricked them, saying, "The Xiongnu envoy came several days ago—where is he now?"

sentences.zh: 」侍胡惶恐曰：「到已三日，去此三十里。

translations.literal: " The attending Hu in fear said: "He arrived three days ago; thirty li from here."
translations.idiomatic: " The Hu attendants said in terror, "He arrived three days ago, thirty li from here."

sentences.zh: 」超乃閉侍胡，悉會其吏士三十六人，與共飲，酒酣，因激怒之曰：「卿曹與我俱在絕域，今虜使到才數日，而王廣禮敬即廢。

translations.literal: " Chao then shut in the Xiongnu attendants, gathered all his clerks and soldiers, thirty-six men, and drank with them; when wine was deep he roused them, saying: "You and I are all in a remote land; the barbarian envoys arrived only days ago, yet King Guang's courtesy and respect were at once abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: " Chao then shut in the Xiongnu attendants, gathered all his clerks and soldiers—thirty-six men—and drank with them; when the wine had gone deep he roused them, saying, "You and I are all in a remote land; the barbarian envoys arrived only days ago, yet King Guang's courtesy and respect were at once abandoned.

sentences.zh: 如令善阜善收吾屬送匈奴，骸骨長為豺狼食矣。

translations.literal: If Shanshan should seize our party and hand us to the Xiongnu, our bones would long be food for wolves and jackals.
translations.idiomatic: If Shanshan should seize our party and hand us to the Xiongnu, our bones would long be food for wolves and jackals.

sentences.zh: 為之奈何？

translations.literal: What is to be done about this?
translations.idiomatic: What is to be done about this?"

sentences.zh: 」官屬皆曰：「今在危亡之地，死生從司馬！

translations.literal: " The officials all said: "We are now in a land of peril and ruin—life and death follow the Acting Major!"
translations.idiomatic: " The officials all said, "We are now in a land of peril and ruin—life and death follow the Acting Major!"

sentences.zh: 」超曰：「不入虎穴，不得虎子。

translations.literal: " Chao said: "If you do not enter the tiger's den, you cannot get the tiger cub.
translations.idiomatic: " Chao said, "If you do not enter the tiger's den, you cannot get the tiger cub.

sentences.zh: 當今之計，獨有因夜以火攻虜，使彼不知我多少，必大震怖，可殄盡也。

translations.literal: The plan for the present is only to take advantage of night and attack the barbarians with fire, so they will not know how many we are—they will surely be greatly shaken and terrified and can be utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The plan for the present is only to take advantage of night and attack the barbarians with fire, so they will not know how many we are—they will surely be greatly shaken and terrified and can be utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 滅此虜，則善阜善破膽，功成事立矣。

translations.literal: Destroy these barbarians and Shanshan will lose its gall—merit accomplished, the enterprise established.
translations.idiomatic: Destroy these barbarians and Shanshan will lose its nerve—merit accomplished, the enterprise established."

sentences.zh: 」眾曰：「當與從事議之。

translations.literal: " The crowd said: "We ought to discuss it with the Attending Clerk."
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd said, "We ought to discuss it with the Attending Clerk."

sentences.zh: 」超怒曰：「吉凶決於今日！

translations.literal: " Chao angrily said: "Fortune and doom are decided today!"
translations.idiomatic: " Chao angrily said, "Fortune and doom are decided today!"

sentences.zh: 從事文俗吏，聞此必恐而謀洩，死無所名，非壯士也。

translations.literal: The Attending Clerk is a civil, conventional official—hear this and he will surely fear and the plot leak; death with no name to leave—no true stalwart.
translations.idiomatic: The Attending Clerk is a civil, conventional official—hear this and he will surely fear and the plot will leak; to die leaving no name is not the act of a true stalwart.

sentences.zh: 」眾曰：「善！

translations.literal: " The crowd said: "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd said, "Good!"

sentences.zh: 」初夜，超遂將吏士往奔虜營。

translations.literal: " At first watch Chao led clerks and soldiers in a rush to the barbarian camp.
translations.idiomatic: " At first watch Chao led clerks and soldiers in a rush to the barbarian camp.

sentences.zh: 會天大風，超令十人持鼓藏虜捨後，約曰：「見火然，皆當鳴鼓大呼。

translations.literal: It happened that a great wind arose; Chao ordered ten men to hold drums and hide behind the barbarians' quarters, agreeing: "When you see fire break out, all must beat drums and shout loudly.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that a great wind arose; Chao ordered ten men to hold drums and hide behind the barbarians' quarters, agreeing, "When you see fire break out, all must beat drums and shout loudly.

sentences.zh: 」餘人悉持兵弩，夾門而伏，超乃順風縱火。

translations.literal: " The rest all held arms and crossbows and lay in ambush flanking the gate; Chao then let fire run with the wind.
translations.idiomatic: " The rest all held arms and crossbows and lay in ambush flanking the gate; Chao then let fire run with the wind.

sentences.zh: 前後鼓噪，虜眾驚亂。

translations.literal: Drums and clamor before and behind—the barbarian masses were alarmed and thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Drums and clamor before and behind—the barbarian masses were alarmed and thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 超手格殺三人，吏兵斬其使及從士三十餘級，餘眾百許人悉燒死。

translations.literal: Chao with his hands struck and killed three men; clerks and soldiers beheaded the envoy and attendants, more than thirty heads; the rest, some hundred-odd men, were all burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Chao with his own hands struck and killed three men; clerks and soldiers beheaded the envoy and attendants, more than thirty heads; the rest, some hundred-odd men, were all burned to death.

sentences.zh: 明日乃還，告郭恂，恂大驚，既而色動，超知其意，舉手曰：「掾雖不行，班超何心獨擅之乎！

translations.literal: The next day he returned and reported to Guo Xun; Xun was greatly alarmed, then his expression shifted; Chao knew his thought and raised his hand, saying: "Though the clerk did not go, how could Ban Chao's heart monopolize the merit alone!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day he returned and reported to Guo Xun; Xun was greatly alarmed, then his expression shifted; Chao knew his thought and raised his hand, saying, "Though the clerk did not go, how could Ban Chao's heart monopolize the merit alone!"

sentences.zh: 」恂乃悅。

translations.literal: " Xun was then pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Xun was then pleased.

sentences.zh: 超於是召善阜善王廣，以虜使首示之，一國震怖。

translations.literal: Chao thereupon summoned King Guang of Shanshan and showed him the barbarian envoys' heads—the whole state trembled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Chao thereupon summoned King Guang of Shanshan and showed him the barbarian envoys' heads—the whole state trembled in terror.

sentences.zh: 超告以漢威德，「自今以後，勿復與北虜通。

translations.literal: Chao informed him of Han's authority and virtue: "From now on, do not again communicate with the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Chao informed him of Han's authority and virtue, "From now on, do not again communicate with the northern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 」廣叩頭：「願屬漢，無二心。

translations.literal: " Guang knocked his head: "I wish to belong to Han, with no second heart.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang knocked his head and said, "I wish to belong to Han, with no second heart.

sentences.zh: 」遂納子為質。

translations.literal: " He thereupon sent his son as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon sent his son as hostage.

sentences.zh: 還白竇固，固大喜，具上超功效，並求更選使使西域。

translations.literal: Returning he reported to Dou Gu; Gu was greatly pleased, fully reported Chao's achievements above, and also requested to select another envoy to send to the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he reported to Dou Gu; Gu was greatly pleased, fully reported Chao's achievements above, and also requested that another envoy be selected to send to the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「吏如班超，何故不遣，而更選乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "An official like Ban Chao—why not send him and instead choose another!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "An official like Ban Chao—why not send him and instead choose another!"

sentences.zh: 今以超為軍司馬，令遂前功。

translations.literal: Now make Chao Army Major and order him to continue his former merit.
translations.idiomatic: Now make Chao Army Major and order him to continue his former merit.

sentences.zh: 固復使超使於窴，欲益其兵，超願但將本所從三十六人，曰：「於窴國大而遠，今將數百人，無益於強；

translations.literal: Gu again sent Chao as envoy to Yutian and wished to increase his troops; Chao wished only to lead the original thirty-six who had followed him, saying: "Yutian's state is large and far; now to lead several hundred men is of no benefit to strength;
translations.idiomatic: Gu again sent Chao as envoy to Yutian and wished to increase his troops; Chao wished only to lead the original thirty-six who had followed him, saying, "Yutian's state is large and far; to lead several hundred men now is of no benefit to strength;

sentences.zh: 如有不虞，多益為累耳。

translations.literal: if something unforeseen occurs, adding more only becomes a burden.
translations.idiomatic: if something unforeseen occurs, adding more only becomes a burden."

sentences.zh: 」是時於窴王廣德雄張南道，而匈奴遣使監護其國。

translations.literal: " At this time King Guangde of Yutian held the southern road in proud sway, and the Xiongnu sent envoys to oversee his state.
translations.idiomatic: " At this time King Guangde of Yutian held the southern road in proud sway, and the Xiongnu sent envoys to oversee his state.

sentences.zh: 超既至於窴，廣德禮意甚疏。

translations.literal: When Chao had reached Yutian, Guangde's courtesy and intent were very slight.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao had reached Yutian, Guangde's courtesy and intent were very slight.

sentences.zh: 且其俗信巫，巫言：「神怒，何故欲向漢？

translations.literal: Moreover their custom trusted shamans; a shaman said: "The spirits are angry—why do you wish to turn toward Han?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover their custom trusted shamans; a shaman said, "The spirits are angry—why do you wish to turn toward Han?

sentences.zh: 漢使有□咼馬，急求取以祠我！

translations.literal: The Han envoy has a □咼 horse—hurry and seek it to sacrifice to me!
translations.idiomatic: The Han envoy has a piebald horse—hurry and seek it to sacrifice to me!"

sentences.zh: 」廣德乃遣國相私來比就超請馬。

translations.literal: " Guangde thereupon sent the state chancellor to come in person privately and approach Chao to request the horse.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangde thereupon sent the state chancellor to come in person privately and approach Chao to request the horse.

sentences.zh: 超密知其狀，報許之，而令巫自來取馬。

translations.literal: Chao secretly knew the situation, replied that he agreed, but ordered the shaman to come himself to take the horse.
translations.idiomatic: Chao secretly knew the situation, replied that he agreed, but ordered the shaman to come himself to take the horse.

sentences.zh: 有頃，巫至，超即斬其首；

translations.literal: Before long the shaman arrived; Chao at once cut off his head;
translations.idiomatic: Before long the shaman arrived; Chao at once cut off his head;

sentences.zh: 收私來比，鞭笞數百。

translations.literal: seized the one who had come in person and flogged him several hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: seized the chancellor who had come in person and flogged him several hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 以巫首送廣德；

translations.literal: He sent the shaman's head to Guangde;
translations.idiomatic: He sent the shaman's head to Guangde;

sentences.zh: 因責讓之。

translations.literal: and thereby rebuked and reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: and thereby rebuked and reproached him.

sentences.zh: 廣德素聞超在善阜善誅滅虜使，大惶恐，即殺匈奴使者而降。

translations.literal: Guangde had long heard that Chao at Shanshan executed and destroyed the barbarian envoys; he was greatly fearful and alarmed, at once killed the Xiongnu envoys and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guangde had long heard that Chao at Shanshan executed and destroyed the barbarian envoys; he was greatly fearful and alarmed, at once killed the Xiongnu envoys and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 超重賜其王以下，因鎮撫焉。

translations.literal: Chao richly rewarded the king and those below, and thereby pacified and settled them.
translations.idiomatic: Chao richly rewarded the king and those below, and thereby pacified and settled them.

sentences.zh: 於是諸國皆遣子入侍，西域與漢絕六十五載，至是乃復通焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various states all sent sons to attend court; the Western Regions and Han had been cut off for sixty-five years—to this time they were again connected.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the various states all sent sons to attend court; the Western Regions and Han had been cut off for sixty-five years—to this time they were again connected.

sentences.zh: 超，彪之子也。

translations.literal: Chao was the son of Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was the son of Biao.

sentences.zh: 淮陽王延，性驕奢，而遇下嚴烈。

translations.literal: Prince Yan of Huaiyang was by nature arrogant and extravagant, yet toward subordinates severe and harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yan of Huaiyang was by nature arrogant and extravagant, yet toward subordinates severe and harsh.

sentences.zh: 有上書告「延與姬兄謝弇及姊婿韓光招奸猾，作圖讖，祠祭祝詛。

translations.literal: Someone submitted a memorial reporting: "Yan with his concubine's elder brother Xie Yan and his elder sister's son-in-law Han Guang recruited crafty villains, made chart-prophecies, and offered sacrifices with curses and imprecations.
translations.idiomatic: Someone submitted a memorial reporting that Yan, with his concubine's elder brother Xie Yan and his elder sister's son-in-law Han Guang, recruited crafty villains, made chart-prophecies, and offered sacrifices with curses and imprecations."

sentences.zh: 事下案驗。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down for investigation and verification.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was sent down for investigation and verification.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸丑，弇、光及司徒邢穆皆坐死，所連及死、徙者甚眾。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on guichou, Xie Yan, Han Guang, and Minister of Education Xing Mu were all punished with death; those implicated who died or were banished were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guichou, Xie Yan, Han Guang, and Minister of Education Xing Mu were all punished with death; those implicated who died or were banished were very numerous.

sentences.zh: 戊午晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On the last day of the month, wuwu, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the month, wuwu day, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙寅，以大司農西河王敏為司徒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingyin, made Grand Minister of Agriculture Wang Min of Xihe Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingyin, Grand Minister of Agriculture Wang Min of Xihe was made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 有司奏請誅淮陽王延，上以延罪薄於楚王英，秋，七月，徙延為阜陵王，食二縣。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized requesting execution of Prince Yan of Huaiyang; the emperor, because Yan's crime was lighter than Prince Ying of Chu's, in autumn, the seventh month, transferred Yan to Prince of Fuling, with revenue from two counties.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices memorialized requesting execution of Prince Yan of Huaiyang; the emperor, because Yan's crime was lighter than Prince Ying of Chu's, in autumn, the seventh month, transferred Yan to Prince of Fuling, with revenue from two counties.

sentences.zh: 是歲，北匈奴大入雲中，雲中太守廉范拒之；

translations.literal: This year the Northern Xiongnu raided deeply into Yunzhong; Administrator of Yunzhong Lian Fan resisted them;
translations.idiomatic: This year the Northern Xiongnu raided deeply into Yunzhong; Administrator of Yunzhong Lian Fan resisted them;

sentences.zh: 吏以眾少，欲移書傍郡求救，范不許。

translations.literal: the clerks, because their numbers were few, wished to send documents to neighboring commanderies to seek rescue; Fan would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: the clerks, because their numbers were few, wished to send documents to neighboring commanderies to seek rescue; Fan would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，范令軍士各交縛兩炬，三頭爇火，營中星列。

translations.literal: It happened to be sunset; Fan ordered the soldiers each to bind two torches crosswise, light fire at three heads—the camp like stars in array.
translations.idiomatic: It happened to be sunset; Fan ordered the soldiers each to bind two torches crosswise, light fire at three heads—the camp like stars in array.

sentences.zh: 虜謂漢兵救至，大驚，待旦將退。

translations.literal: The barbarians thought Han troops had arrived to rescue and were greatly alarmed; they waited for dawn and were about to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians thought Han rescue troops had arrived and were greatly alarmed; they waited for dawn and were about to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 范令軍中蓐食，晨，往赴之，斬

translations.literal: Fan ordered the army to take mat-meals; at dawn he went to meet them and beheaded
translations.idiomatic: Fan ordered the army to take mat-meals; at dawn he went to meet them and beheaded

sentences.zh: 首數百級，虜自相轔藉，死者千餘人，由此不敢復向雲中。

translations.literal: several hundred heads; the barbarians trampled one another—more than a thousand dead; from this they did not again dare turn toward Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: several hundred heads; the barbarians trampled one another—more than a thousand dead; from this they did not again dare turn toward Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 范，丹之孫也。

translations.literal: Fan was the grandson of Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was the grandson of Dan.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，上當謁原陵，夜，夢先帝、太后如平生歡，既寤，悲不能寐；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the emperor was to attend Yuanling; at night he dreamed the former emperor and empress dowager as in life in joy; when he awoke he grieved and could not sleep;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the emperor was to attend Yuanling; at night he dreamed the former emperor and empress dowager as in life in joy; when he awoke he grieved and could not sleep;

sentences.zh: 即案歷，明旦日吉，遂率百官上陵。

translations.literal: he at once examined the calendar—the next day's day was auspicious—and thereupon led the hundred officials to ascend the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: he at once examined the calendar—the next day was auspicious—and thereupon led the hundred officials to ascend the tomb.

sentences.zh: 其日，降甘露於陵樹，帝令百官採取以薦。

translations.literal: That day sweet dew descended on the tomb trees; the emperor ordered the hundred officials to gather it for offering.
translations.idiomatic: That day sweet dew descended on the tomb trees; the emperor ordered the hundred officials to gather it for offering.

sentences.zh: 會畢，帝從席前伏御床，視太后鏡奩中物，感動悲涕，令易脂澤裝具；

translations.literal: When the assembly ended the emperor from before the mat prostrated himself on the imperial couch, looked at objects in the empress dowager's mirror casket, was moved and wept in grief, and ordered fresh rouge and adornments replaced;
translations.idiomatic: When the assembly ended the emperor from before the mat prostrated himself on the imperial couch, looked at objects in the empress dowager's mirror casket, was moved and wept in grief, and ordered fresh rouge and adornments replaced;

sentences.zh: 左右皆泣，莫能仰視。

translations.literal: those at his sides all wept and none could look up.
translations.idiomatic: those at his sides all wept and none could look up.

sentences.zh: 北海敬王睦薨。

translations.literal: Prince Mu the Respectful of Beihai died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mu the Respectful of Beihai died.

sentences.zh: 睦少好學，光武及上皆愛之，嘗遣中大夫詣京師朝賀，召而謂之曰：「朝廷設問寡人，大夫將何辭以對？

translations.literal: Mu from youth loved learning; Guangwu and the emperor both cherished him; he was once sent with a Palace Grandee to the capital for New Year congratulations; summoned and told him: "If the court sets questions to me, what words will the grandee use to reply?
translations.idiomatic: Mu from youth loved learning; Guangwu and the emperor both cherished him; he was once sent with a Palace Grandee to the capital for New Year congratulations; summoned and told him, "If the court sets questions to me, what words will the grandee use to reply?

sentences.zh: 」使者曰：「大王忠孝慈仁，敬賢樂士，臣敢不以實對！

translations.literal: " The envoy said: "The great king is loyal, filial, kind, and benevolent, respects the worthy and delights in scholars—your servant dares not reply otherwise than in truth!"
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy said, "The great king is loyal, filial, kind, and benevolent, respects the worthy and delights in scholars—I dare not reply otherwise than in truth!"

sentences.zh: 」睦曰：「吁，子危我哉！

translations.literal: " Mu said: "Alas, you endanger me!"
translations.idiomatic: " Mu said, "Alas, you endanger me!"

sentences.zh: 此乃孤幼時進趣之行也。

translations.literal: Those are my youthful pursuits when young.
translations.idiomatic: Those are my youthful pursuits when young.

sentences.zh: 大夫其對以孤襲爵以來，志意衰惰，聲色是娛，犬馬是好，乃為相愛耳。

translations.literal: Let the grandee reply that since I inherited the fief my will and intent have declined and grown slack, sound and color are my pleasure, dogs and horses are my delight—that is what will show mutual affection.
translations.idiomatic: Let the grandee reply that since I inherited the fief my will and intent have declined and grown slack, sound and color are my pleasure, dogs and horses are my delight—that is what will show mutual affection."

sentences.zh: 」其智慮畏慎如此。

translations.literal: " His wisdom and caution were thus.
translations.idiomatic: " His wisdom and caution were thus.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙巳，司徒王敏薨。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yisi, Minister of Education Wang Min died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yisi, Minister of Education Wang Min died.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸丑，以汝南太守鮑昱為司徒。

translations.literal: In the third month, on guichou, made Administrator of Runan Bao Yu Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guichou, Administrator of Runan Bao Yu was made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 昱，永之子也。

translations.literal: Yu was the son of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was the son of Yong.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史梁國朱輔宣示漢德，威懷遠夷，自汶山以西，前世所不至，正朔所未加，白狼、槃木等百餘國。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yi Province Zhu Fu of Liangguo proclaimed Han's virtue; by awesomeness he embraced distant barbarians—from Mount Wen westward, places former ages never reached, where the calendar and regalia had not been applied, the Bailang, Panmu, and more than a hundred states.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yi Province Zhu Fu of Liangguo proclaimed Han's virtue; by awesomeness he embraced distant barbarians—from Mount Wen westward, places former ages never reached, where the calendar and regalia had not been applied, the Bailang, Panmu, and more than a hundred states.

sentences.zh: 皆舉種稱臣奉貢。

translations.literal: All raised their tribes to style themselves subjects and present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: All raised their tribes to style themselves subjects and present tribute.

sentences.zh: 白狼王唐取作詩三章，歌頌漢德，輔使犍為郡掾由恭譯而獻之。

translations.literal: King Tang Qu of the Bailang composed three stanzas of verse praising Han's virtue; Fu had You Gong, clerk of Qianwei commandery, translate and present them.
translations.idiomatic: King Tang Qu of the Bailang composed three stanzas of verse praising Han's virtue; Fu had You Gong, clerk of Qianwei commandery, translate and present them.

sentences.zh: 初，龜茲王建為匈奴所立，倚恃虜威，據有北道，攻殺疏勒王，立其臣兜題為疏勒王。

translations.literal: At first King Jian of Kucha was established by the Xiongnu; relying on barbarian might he held the northern road, attacked and killed the king of Shule, and established his minister Douti as king of Shule.
translations.idiomatic: At first King Jian of Kucha was established by the Xiongnu; relying on barbarian might he held the northern road, attacked and killed the king of Shule, and established his minister Douti as king of Shule.

sentences.zh: 班超從間道至疏勒，去兜題所居槃橐城九十里，逆遣吏田慮先往降之，敕慮曰：「兜題本非疏勒種，國人必不用命；

translations.literal: Ban Chao by a side road reached Shule, ninety li from Pantuo city where Douti dwelt; he sent ahead Clerk Tian Lü to go first and induce surrender, instructing Lü: "Douti is originally not of Shule stock—the people will surely not obey his commands;
translations.idiomatic: Ban Chao by a side road reached Shule, ninety li from Pantuo city where Douti dwelt; he sent ahead Clerk Tian Lü to go first and induce surrender, instructing Lü, "Douti is originally not of Shule stock—the people will surely not obey his commands;

sentences.zh: 若不即降，便可執之。

translations.literal: if he does not surrender at once, you may seize him.
translations.idiomatic: if he does not surrender at once, you may seize him."

sentences.zh: 」慮既到，兜題見慮輕弱，殊無降意。

translations.literal: " When Lü had arrived, Douti saw Lü was slight and weak and had absolutely no intent to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " When Lü had arrived, Douti saw Lü was slight and weak and had absolutely no intent to surrender.

sentences.zh: 慮因其無備，遂前劫縛兜題，左右出其不意，皆驚懼奔走。

translations.literal: Lü, because he was unprepared, thereupon advanced and seized and bound Douti; those at his sides, caught unawares, all fled in alarm and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Lü, because Douti was unprepared, thereupon advanced and seized and bound him; those at his sides, caught unawares, all fled in alarm and fear.

sentences.zh: 慮馳報超，超即赴之，悉召疏勒將吏，說以龜茲無道之狀，因立其故王兄子忠為王，國人大悅。

translations.literal: Lü galloped to report to Chao; Chao at once hastened there, summoned all Shule's generals and officials, explained Kucha's lawless conduct, and thereby established the former king's elder brother's son Zhong as king—the state's people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Lü galloped to report to Chao; Chao at once hastened there, summoned all Shule's generals and officials, explained Kucha's lawless conduct, and thereby established the former king's elder brother's son Zhong as king—the state's people were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 超問忠及官屬：「當殺兜題邪，生遣之邪？

translations.literal: Chao asked Zhong and the officials: "Should we kill Douti, or send him away alive?
translations.idiomatic: Chao asked Zhong and the officials, "Should we kill Douti, or send him away alive?

sentences.zh: 」鹹曰：「當殺之。

translations.literal: " All said: "He should be killed."
translations.idiomatic: " All said, "He should be killed."

sentences.zh: 」超曰；

translations.literal: " Chao said;
translations.idiomatic: " Chao said,

sentences.zh: 「殺之無益於事，當令龜茲知漢威德。

translations.literal: "To kill him is of no benefit to the affair—we should let Kucha know Han's authority and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: "To kill him is of no benefit to the affair—we should let Kucha know Han's authority and virtue.

sentences.zh: 」遂解遣之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon released and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon released and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，戊子，公卿百官以帝威德懷遠，祥物顯應，並集朝堂奉觴上壽。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on wuzi, the Excellencies, ministers, and hundred officials, because the emperor's authority and virtue embraced the distant and auspicious things appeared in response, all gathered in the court hall, raised cups, and offered longevity.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on wuzi, the Excellencies, ministers, and hundred officials, because the emperor's authority and virtue embraced the distant and auspicious things appeared in response, all gathered in the court hall, raised cups, and offered longevity.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「天生神物，以應王者；

translations.literal: An edict said: "Heaven produces numinous things to respond to kings;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Heaven produces numinous things to respond to kings;

sentences.zh: 遠人慕化，實由有德；

translations.literal: distant people admire transformation—truly because of possessing virtue;
translations.idiomatic: distant people admire transformation—truly because of possessing virtue;

sentences.zh: 朕以虛薄，何以享斯！

translations.literal: I am empty and slight—how can I enjoy this!
translations.idiomatic: I am empty and slight—how can I enjoy this!

sentences.zh: 唯高祖、光武聖德所被，不敢有辭，其敬舉觴，太常擇吉日策告宗廟。

translations.literal: Only what Gaozu and Guangwu's sagely virtue overspread—I dare not decline; respectfully raise your cups; the Grand Master of Ceremonies shall choose an auspicious day and report by written proclamation to the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Only what Gaozu and Guangwu's sagely virtue overspread—I dare not decline; respectfully raise your cups; the Grand Master of Ceremonies shall choose an auspicious day and report by written proclamation to the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 」仍推恩賜民爵及粟有差。

translations.literal: " He still extended grace and bestowed ranks and grain on the people in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: " He still extended grace and bestowed ranks and grain on the people in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，遣奉車都尉竇固、駙馬都尉耿秉、騎都尉劉張出敦煌崑崙塞，擊西域，秉、張皆去符，傳以屬固，合兵萬四千騎，擊破白山虜於蒲類海上，遂進擊車師。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, sent Bearer of the Imperial Carriage Dou Gu, Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law Geng Bing, and Commandant of Cavalry Liu Zhang out through Dunhuang and the Kunlun Pass to strike the Western Regions; Bing and Zhang both removed their tallies and passed authority to Gu; combined troops fourteen thousand horse; routed the Baishan barbarians at Pulei Sea and thereupon advanced to strike Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, Bearer of the Imperial Carriage Dou Gu, Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law Geng Bing, and Commandant of Cavalry Liu Zhang were sent out through Dunhuang and the Kunlun Pass to strike the Western Regions; Bing and Zhang both removed their tallies and passed authority to Gu; combined troops numbered fourteen thousand horse; they routed the Baishan barbarians at Pulei Sea and thereupon advanced to strike Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 車師前王，即後王之子也，其廷相去五百餘里。

translations.literal: The Front King of Cheshi was the son of the Rear King; their courts were more than five hundred li apart.
translations.idiomatic: The Front King of Cheshi was the son of the Rear King; their courts were more than five hundred li apart.

sentences.zh: 固以後王道遠，山谷深，士卒寒苦，欲攻前王；

translations.literal: Gu, because the Rear King's road was far, valleys deep, and soldiers cold and suffering, wished to attack the Front King;
translations.idiomatic: Gu, because the Rear King's road was far, valleys deep, and soldiers cold and suffering, wished to attack the Front King;

sentences.zh: 秉以為先赴後王，並力根本，則前王自服。

translations.literal: Bing held that if they first hastened to the Rear King and combined strength at the root, the Front King would submit of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Bing held that if they first hastened to the Rear King and combined strength at the root, the Front King would submit of himself.

sentences.zh: 固計未決，秉奮身而起曰：「請行前。

translations.literal: Gu's plan was undecided; Bing roused himself and rose, saying: "I request to go ahead."
translations.idiomatic: Gu's plan was undecided; Bing roused himself and rose, saying, "I request to go ahead."

sentences.zh: 」乃上馬引兵北入，眾軍不得已，並進，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: " He thereupon mounted, led troops northward in, and the mass of armies had no choice but to advance together and behead several thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon mounted, led troops northward, and the mass of armies had no choice but to advance together and behead several thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 後王安得震怖，走出門迎秉，脫帽，抱馬足降，秉將以詣固；

translations.literal: The Rear King An was shaken and terrified, went out the gate to meet Bing, removed his cap, embraced the horse's legs and surrendered; Bing was about to bring him to Gu;
translations.idiomatic: The Rear King An was shaken and terrified, went out the gate to meet Bing, removed his cap, embraced the horse's legs and surrendered; Bing was about to bring him to Gu;

sentences.zh: 其前王亦歸命，遂定車師而還。

translations.literal: the Front King also submitted; they thereupon settled Cheshi and returned.
translations.idiomatic: the Front King also submitted; they thereupon settled Cheshi and returned.

sentences.zh: 於是固奏復置西域都護及戊、己校尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gu memorialized to restore the Protector of the Western Regions and the Geng and Ji commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Gu memorialized to restore the Protector of the Western Regions and the Geng and Ji commandants.

sentences.zh: 以陳睦為都護；

translations.literal: Chen Mu was made Protector;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mu was made Protector;

sentences.zh: 司馬耿恭為戊校尉，屯後王部金蒲城；

translations.literal: Major Geng Gong was made Colonel of the Wuji Garrison and encamped at Jinpucheng in the Rear King's territory;
translations.idiomatic: Major Geng Gong was made Colonel of the Wuji Garrison and encamped at Jinpucheng in the Rear King's territory;

sentences.zh: 謁者關寵為己校尉，屯前王部柳中城，屯各置數百人。

translations.literal: Gentleman-Usher Guan Chong was made Colonel of the Jiyi Garrison and encamped at Liuzhong in the Front King's territory; each garrison was posted with several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman-Usher Guan Chong was made Colonel of the Jiyi Garrison and encamped at Liuzhong in the Front King's territory; each garrison was posted with several hundred men.

sentences.zh: 恭，況之孫也。

translations.literal: Gong was the grandson of Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was the grandson of Geng Kuang.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，詔竇固等罷兵還京師。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, an edict ordered Dou Gu and the others to dismiss the army and return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, an edict ordered Dou Gu and the others to dismiss the army and return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 北單于遣左鹿蠡王率二萬騎擊車師，耿恭遣司馬將兵三百人救之，皆為所沒，匈奴遂破殺車師後王安得而攻金蒲城。

translations.literal: The Northern Chanyu sent the Left Luli King with twenty thousand horse to attack Cheshi; Geng Gong sent a major with three hundred troops to rescue them—all were destroyed by the enemy; the Xiongnu thereupon broke and killed the Rear King of Cheshi An De and attacked Jinpucheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Chanyu sent the Left Luli King with twenty thousand horse to attack Cheshi; Geng Gong sent a major with three hundred troops to rescue them—all were destroyed; the Xiongnu thereupon broke and killed the Rear King of Cheshi An De and attacked Jinpucheng.

sentences.zh: 恭以毒藥傅矢，語匈奴曰：「漢家箭神，其中瘡者必有異。

translations.literal: Gong smeared poison on arrows and told the Xiongnu: "Han arrows are divine—whoever is struck in the wound will surely have something strange happen.
translations.idiomatic: Gong smeared poison on the arrows and told the Xiongnu, "Han arrows are divine—whoever is struck in the wound will surely suffer something strange.

sentences.zh: 」虜中矢者，視創皆沸，大驚，會天暴風雨，隨雨擊之，殺傷甚眾；

translations.literal: " Among the barbarians those struck by arrows saw their wounds all boil; they were greatly alarmed; just then Heaven sent violent wind and rain, and following the rain they struck them, killing and wounding very many;
translations.idiomatic: " Among the barbarians those struck by arrows saw their wounds boil; they were greatly alarmed; just then a violent storm broke, and they struck them amid the rain, killing and wounding very many;

sentences.zh: 匈奴震怖，相謂曰：「漢兵神，真可畏也！

translations.literal: the Xiongnu were shaken in terror and said to one another: "Han troops are divine—truly to be feared!
translations.idiomatic: the Xiongnu were shaken in terror and said to one another, "Han troops are divine—truly to be feared!"

sentences.zh: 」遂解去。

translations.literal: " They thereupon raised the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They thereupon raised the siege and departed.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，己未，有星孛於太微。

translations.literal: In summer, the sixth month, on day jiwei, a comet appeared in the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, on jiwei day, a comet appeared in the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 耿恭以疏勒城傍有澗水可固，引兵據之。

translations.literal: Geng Gong because beside Shule city there was stream water by which one could make a stand led his troops to occupy it.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Gong, because stream water beside Shule city could serve for a stand, led his troops to occupy it.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，匈奴復來攻，擁絕澗水；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Xiongnu came again to attack and blocked off the stream water;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the Xiongnu came again to attack and blocked off the stream water;

sentences.zh: 恭於城中穿井十五丈，不得水，吏士渴乏，至笮馬糞汁而飲之。

translations.literal: Gong within the city dug a well fifteen zhang deep but obtained no water; officers and soldiers were parched and exhausted, reaching the point of squeezing horse dung for juice to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Gong dug a well fifteen zhang deep within the city but obtained no water; officers and soldiers were parched and exhausted, reaching the point of squeezing horse dung for juice to drink.

sentences.zh: 恭身自率士挽籠，有頃，水泉奔出，眾皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Gong in person led the soldiers to draw with buckets; in a moment a spring burst forth and all cried "Long live the ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Gong in person led the soldiers to draw with buckets; in a moment a spring burst forth and all cried "Long live!"

sentences.zh: 乃令吏士揚水以示虜，虜出不意，以為神明，遂引去。

translations.literal: He then ordered officers and soldiers to splash water to show the barbarians; the barbarians, not expecting it, took it for divine power and thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered officers and soldiers to splash water to show the barbarians; the barbarians, not expecting it, took it for divine power and thereupon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬子，帝崩於東宮前殿，年四十八。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day renzi, the Emperor died in the front hall of the Eastern Palace, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renzi day, the Emperor died in the front hall of the Eastern Palace, aged forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 遺詔：「無起寢廟，藏主於光烈皇后更衣別室。

translations.literal: His testamentary edict said: "Do not raise a sleeping temple; store the spirit tablet in Empress Guanglie's dressing-room side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: His testamentary edict said, "Do not raise a sleeping temple; store the spirit tablet in Empress Guanglie's dressing-room side chamber."

sentences.zh: 」帝遵奉建武制度，無所變更，后妃之家不得封侯與政。

translations.literal: " The Emperor had followed and upheld the Jianwu institutions without any change; families of empresses and consorts were not permitted enfeoffment as marquises or participation in government.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had followed and upheld the Jianwu institutions without change; families of empresses and consorts were not permitted enfeoffment as marquises or participation in government.

sentences.zh: 館陶公主為子求郎，不許，而賜錢千萬，謂群臣曰：「郎官上應列宿，出宰百里，苟非其人，則民受其殃，是以難之。

translations.literal: The Princess of Guantao sought a Gentleman-attendant post for her son; he did not permit it but bestowed ten million cash, saying to the ministers: "Gentleman-attendants above correspond to the arrayed stars; going out they govern a hundred li—if the man is not right, the people suffer their calamity; that is why it is hard.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Guantao sought a Gentleman-attendant post for her son; he did not permit it but bestowed ten million cash, saying to the ministers, "Gentleman-attendants above correspond to the arrayed stars; going out they govern a hundred li—if the man is not right, the people suffer calamity; that is why it is hard."

sentences.zh: 」公車以反支日不受章奏，帝聞而怪曰：「民廢農桑，遠來詣闕，而復拘以禁忌，豈為政之意乎！

translations.literal: " The Imperial Carriage Office on fanzhi days did not accept memorials and reports; the Emperor heard of it and said in wonder: "The people abandon farming and sericulture and come from afar to the palace gate, yet you again bind them with taboos—is this the intent of government!
translations.idiomatic: " The Imperial Carriage Office on fanzhi days did not accept memorials and reports; the Emperor heard of it and said in wonder, "The people abandon farming and sericulture and come from afar to the palace gate, yet you again bind them with taboos—is this the intent of government!"

sentences.zh: 」於是遂蠲其制。

translations.literal: " He thereupon abolished that regulation.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon abolished that regulation.

sentences.zh: 尚書閻章二妹為貴人，章精力曉舊典，久次當遷重職，帝為後宮親屬，竟不用。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Yan Zhang's two younger sisters were Worthy Ladies; Zhang was energetic and understood old regulations; long in rank he ought to have been promoted to a weighty post—the Emperor because he was kin of the rear palace ultimately did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Master of Writing Yan Zhang's two younger sisters were Worthy Ladies; Zhang was energetic and understood old regulations; long in rank he ought to have been promoted to a weighty post—the Emperor, because he was kin of the rear palace, ultimately did not employ him.

sentences.zh: 是以吏得其人，民樂其業，遠近畏服，戶口滋殖焉。

translations.literal: Therefore officials obtained the right men, the people rejoiced in their occupations, far and near feared and submitted, and households and population flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore officials obtained the right men, the people rejoiced in their occupations, far and near feared and submitted, and households and population flourished.

sentences.zh: 太子即位，年十八。

translations.literal: The heir apparent assumed the throne, aged eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent assumed the throne, aged eighteen.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后曰皇太后。

translations.literal: The empress was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 明帝初崩，馬氏兄弟爭欲入宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming had just died, the Ma clan brothers strove to enter the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming had just died, the Ma clan brothers strove to enter the palace.

sentences.zh: 北宮衛士令楊仁被甲持戟，嚴勒門衛，人莫敢輕進者。

translations.literal: Commandant of the North Palace Guards Yang Ren donned armor and grasped a halberd, sternly restraining the gate guards—none dared lightly advance.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the North Palace Guards Yang Ren donned armor and grasped a halberd, sternly restraining the gate guards—none dared lightly advance.

sentences.zh: 諸馬乃共譖仁於章帝，言其峻刻。

translations.literal: The various Mas thereupon together slandered Ren to Emperor Zhang, saying he was harsh and severe.
translations.idiomatic: The various Mas thereupon together slandered Ren to Emperor Zhang, saying he was harsh and severe.

sentences.zh: 帝知其忠，愈善之，拜為什邡令。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew his loyalty and favored him all the more, appointing him Magistrate of Shifang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor knew his loyalty and favored him all the more, appointing him Magistrate of Shifang.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，葬孝明皇帝於顯節陵。

translations.literal: On day renxu Emperor Xiao Ming was buried at Xianjie Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day Emperor Xiao Ming was buried at Xianjie Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁未，赦天下。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on day dingwei, there was an amnesty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingwei day, there was an amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 詔以行太尉事節鄉侯熹為太傅，司空融為太尉，並錄尚書事。

translations.literal: An edict made Marquis of Jiexiang Xi, acting as Grand Commandant, Grand Tutor, and Minister of Works Rong Grand Commandant, both recording matters of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Marquis of Jiexiang Zhao Xi, acting as Grand Commandant, Grand Tutor, and Minister of Works Dou Rong Grand Commandant, both recording matters of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊戌，以蜀郡太守第五倫為司空。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on day wuxu, the Administrator of Shu commandery Diwu Lun was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuxu day, the Administrator of Shu commandery Diwu Lun was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 倫在郡公清，所舉吏多得其人，故帝自遠郡用之。

translations.literal: Lun in the commandery was fair and pure; those he recommended as clerks mostly were the right men—therefore the Emperor used him from a distant commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lun in the commandery was fair and pure; those he recommended as clerks mostly were the right men—therefore the Emperor used him from a distant commandery.

sentences.zh: 焉耆、龜茲攻沒都護陳睦，北匈奴圍關寵於柳中城。

translations.literal: Yanqi and Kucha attacked and destroyed Protector of the Western Regions Chen Mu; the Northern Xiongnu besieged Guan Chong at Liuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi and Kucha attacked and destroyed Protector of the Western Regions Chen Mu; the Northern Xiongnu besieged Guan Chong at Liuzhong.

sentences.zh: 會中國有大喪，救兵不至，車師復叛，與匈奴共攻耿恭。

translations.literal: Just then the central state had a great mourning and relief troops did not arrive; Cheshi rebelled again and with the Xiongnu jointly attacked Geng Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the central state had a great mourning and relief troops did not arrive; Cheshi rebelled again and with the Xiongnu jointly attacked Geng Gong.

sentences.zh: 恭率厲士眾御之，數月，食盡窮困，乃煮鎧弩，食其筋革。

translations.literal: Gong led and exhorted officers and masses to defend against them; after several months food was exhausted and they were destitute, and they boiled armor and crossbows and ate their sinew and hide.
translations.idiomatic: Gong led and exhorted officers and troops to defend against them; after several months food was exhausted and they were destitute, and they boiled armor and crossbows and ate their sinew and hide.

sentences.zh: 恭與士卒推誠同死生。

translations.literal: Gong with the soldiers extended sincerity and shared life and death.
translations.idiomatic: Gong with the soldiers extended sincerity and shared life and death.

sentences.zh: 故皆無二心，而稍稍死亡。

translations.literal: Therefore all had no second heart, yet they gradually died off.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore all were of one mind, yet they gradually died off.

sentences.zh: 餘數十人。

translations.literal: Only several tens remained.
translations.idiomatic: Only several tens remained.

sentences.zh: 單于知恭已困，欲必降之，遣使招恭曰：「若降者，當封為白屋王。

translations.literal: The Chanyu knew Gong was already trapped and wished to make him surely submit; he sent envoys to summon Gong, saying: "If you submit, you shall be enfeoffed as King of the White Dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu knew Gong was already trapped and wished to make him surely submit; he sent envoys to summon Gong, saying, "If you submit, you shall be enfeoffed as King of the White Dwelling."

sentences.zh: 妻以女子。

translations.literal: A woman shall be given you as wife.
translations.idiomatic: A woman shall be given you as wife."

sentences.zh: 」恭誘其使上城，手擊殺之，炙諸城上。

translations.literal: " Gong lured their envoys up onto the wall, personally struck and killed them, and roasted them on the wall for all to see.
translations.idiomatic: Gong lured their envoys up onto the wall, personally struck and killed them, and roasted them on the wall for all to see.

sentences.zh: 單于大怒，更益兵圍恭，不能下。

translations.literal: The Chanyu was greatly angered and further increased troops to besiege Gong but could not take him.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu was greatly angered and further increased troops to besiege Gong but could not take him.

sentences.zh: 關寵上書求救。

translations.literal: Guan Chong submitted a memorial seeking rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Chong submitted a memorial seeking rescue.

sentences.zh: 詔公卿會議，司空倫以為不宜救，司徒鮑昱曰：「今使人於危難之地，急而棄之，外則縱蠻夷之暴，內則傷死難之臣，誠令權時，後無邊事可也。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the excellencies and ministers to meet in council; Minister of Works Lun held that rescue was not fitting; Minister of Education Bao Yu said: "Now we have sent men into lands of peril and danger—if in urgency we abandon them, outwardly we indulge the violence of barbarians, inwardly we wound ministers who died in hardship; even if for the moment one weighs expedience, afterward there will be no border affairs possible.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the excellencies and ministers to meet in council; Minister of Works Lun held that rescue was not fitting; Minister of Education Bao Yu said, "Now we have sent men into lands of peril and danger—if in urgency we abandon them, outwardly we indulge barbarian violence, inwardly we wound ministers who died in hardship; even if for the moment one weighs expedience, afterward there will be no border affairs possible."

sentences.zh: 匈奴如復犯塞為寇，陛下將何以使將！

translations.literal: If the Xiongnu again violate the passes as raiders, how will Your Majesty be able to employ generals!
translations.idiomatic: If the Xiongnu again violate the passes as raiders, how will Your Majesty be able to employ generals!"

sentences.zh: 又二部兵人裁各數十，匈奴圍之，歷旬不下，是其寡弱力盡之效也。

translations.literal: Moreover the troops of the two garrisons number barely several tens each; the Xiongnu besiege them yet for ten days cannot take them—this is the effect of their fewness, weakness, and exhausted strength.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the troops of the two garrisons number barely several tens each; the Xiongnu besiege them yet for ten days cannot take them—this is the effect of their fewness, weakness, and exhausted strength.

sentences.zh: 可令敦煌、酒泉太守各將精騎二千，多其幡幟，倍道兼行以赴其急；

translations.literal: One may order the Administrators of Dunhuang and Jiuquan each to lead two thousand picked horse, multiply their banners and flags, and by double marches press on night and day to relieve their urgency;
translations.idiomatic: One may order the Administrators of Dunhuang and Jiuquan each to lead two thousand picked horse, multiply their banners and flags, and by double marches press on night and day to relieve their urgency;

sentences.zh: 匈奴疲極之兵，必不敢當，四十日間足還入塞。

translations.literal: the Xiongnu troops, exhausted to the limit, will surely not dare to oppose them; within forty days it is enough to return inside the passes.
translations.idiomatic: the Xiongnu troops, exhausted to the limit, will surely not dare to oppose them; within forty days it is enough to return inside the passes."

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 乃遣征西將軍耿秉屯酒泉，行太守事，遣酒泉太守段彭與謁者王蒙、皇甫援發張掖、酒泉、敦煌三郡及善阜善兵合七千餘人以救之。

translations.literal: He then sent General Who Conquers the West Geng Bing to encamp at Jiuquan and act as Administrator, and sent Jiuquan Administrator Duan Peng with Gentlemen-Usher Wang Meng and Huangfu Yuan to raise troops from Zhangye, Jiuquan, and Dunhuang commanderies and Shanshan forces—more than seven thousand in all—to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent General Who Conquers the West Geng Bing to encamp at Jiuquan and act as Administrator, and sent Jiuquan Administrator Duan Peng with Gentlemen-Usher Wang Meng and Huangfu Yuan to raise troops from Zhangye, Jiuquan, and Dunhuang commanderies and Shanshan forces—more than seven thousand in all—to rescue them.

sentences.zh: 甲辰晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On the last day of month jiachen there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of jiachen month there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 太后兄弟虎賁中郎廖及黃門郎防、光，終明帝世未嘗改官。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's brothers Huben Central Gentleman Liao and Yellow Gate Gentleman Fang and Guang through Emperor Ming's reign had never had their offices changed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's brothers Huben Central Gentleman Liao and Yellow Gate Gentlemen Fang and Guang through Emperor Ming's reign had never had their offices changed.

sentences.zh: 帝以廖為衛尉，防為中郎將，光為越騎校尉。

translations.literal: The Emperor made Liao Commandant of the Guards, Fang Commandant of the Gentlemen, and Guang Colonel of the Yueqi Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Liao Commandant of the Guards, Fang Commandant of the Gentlemen, and Guang Colonel of the Yueqi Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 廖等傾身交結，冠蓋之士爭赴趣之。

translations.literal: Liao and the others threw themselves wholly into forming connections; gentlemen of caps and coaches strove to hurry to them.
translations.idiomatic: Liao and the others threw themselves wholly into forming connections; gentlemen of caps and coaches strove to hurry to them.

sentences.zh: 第五倫上疏曰：「臣聞《書》曰：『臣無作威作福，其害於而家，凶於而國。

translations.literal: Diwu Lun submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that the Documents says: 'Ministers must not make awesomeness or make blessings—the harm reaches your family, the misfortune reaches your state.
translations.idiomatic: Diwu Lun submitted a memorial, saying, "I have heard that the Documents says, 'Ministers must not make awesomeness or make blessings—the harm reaches your family, the misfortune reaches your state."

sentences.zh: 』近世光烈皇后雖友愛天至，而抑損陰氏，不假以權勢。

translations.literal: ' In recent times Empress Guanglie, though her friendship and love reached Heaven's utmost, yet restrained and reduced the Yin clan and did not lend them power and influence.
translations.idiomatic: ' In recent times Empress Guanglie, though her friendship and love reached Heaven's utmost, yet restrained and reduced the Yin clan and did not lend them power and influence.

sentences.zh: 其後梁、竇之家，互有非法，明帝即位，竟多誅之。

translations.literal: Afterward the Liang and Dou households each had unlawful acts; when Emperor Ming took the throne he in the end executed many of them.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Liang and Dou households each had unlawful acts; when Emperor Ming took the throne he in the end executed many of them.

sentences.zh: 自是雒中無復權戚，書記請托，一皆斷絕。

translations.literal: From this time in Luoyang there were no more powerful kin; written requests and entreaties were all cut off.
translations.idiomatic: From this time in Luoyang there were no more powerful kin; written requests and entreaties were all cut off.

sentences.zh: 又諭諸外戚曰：『苦身待士，不如為國。

translations.literal: He also instructed the various maternal kin: 'To toil the body and wait on scholars is not as good as serving the state.
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed the various maternal kin, 'To toil the body and wait on scholars is not as good as serving the state."

sentences.zh: 戴盆望天，事不兩施。

translations.literal: Wearing a basin on the head while looking at Heaven—two things cannot be done at once.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing a basin on the head while looking at Heaven—two things cannot be done at once."

sentences.zh: 』今之議者，復以馬氏為言。

translations.literal: ' Today's debaters again take the Ma clan as their topic.
translations.idiomatic: ' Today's debaters again take the Ma clan as their topic.

sentences.zh: 竊聞衛尉廖以布三千匹，城門校尉防以錢三百萬，私贍三輔衣冠，知與不知，莫不畢給。

translations.literal: I have heard that Commandant of the Guards Liao with three thousand bolts of cloth and Colonel of the City Gates Fang with three million cash privately supported the caps and robes of the Three Metropolises—whether known to them or not, none failed to receive a full grant.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Commandant of the Guards Liao with three thousand bolts of cloth and Colonel of the City Gates Fang with three million cash privately supported the caps and robes of the Three Metropolises—whether known to them or not, none failed to receive a full grant.

sentences.zh: 又聯臘日亦遺其在雒中者錢各五千。

translations.literal: Moreover on the la festival they also sent those of their kin in Luoyang five thousand cash each.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover on the la festival they also sent those of their kin in Luoyang five thousand cash each.

sentences.zh: 越騎校尉光，臘用羊三百頭，米四百斛，肉五千斤。

translations.literal: Colonel of the Yueqi Cavalry Guang for the la used three hundred sheep, four hundred hu of grain, and five thousand jin of meat.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel of the Yueqi Cavalry Guang for the la used three hundred sheep, four hundred hu of grain, and five thousand jin of meat.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為不應經義。

translations.literal: Your servant in folly holds that this does not accord with canonical meaning.
translations.idiomatic: I in folly hold that this does not accord with canonical meaning.

sentences.zh: 惶恐，不敢不以聞。

translations.literal: In fear and trembling I dare not fail to report it.
translations.idiomatic: In fear and trembling I dare not fail to report it.

sentences.zh: 陛下情慾厚之，亦宜所以安之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's feelings and desires are thick toward them—you also ought thereby to bring them peace.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's feelings are generous toward them—you also ought thereby to bring them peace.

sentences.zh: 臣今言此，誠欲上忠陛下，下全後家也。

translations.literal: Your servant now speaks this truly wishing above to be loyal to Your Majesty and below to preserve the empress's family.
translations.idiomatic: I now speak this truly wishing above to be loyal to Your Majesty and below to preserve the empress's family.

sentences.zh: 是歲，京師及兗、豫、徐州大旱。

translations.literal: This year the capital and Yan, Yu, and Xu provinces suffered great drought.
translations.idiomatic: This year the capital and Yan, Yu, and Xu provinces suffered great drought.
